name: Infant James (given name not recorded)
note: Register p.48 (1857). Levi James (LV0560, 1825-1903) and Martha Ellen Paxson James (LV0561, 1824-1915) lie at C-26 with their children Americus Cauldwell James (b.1852) and Sarah Frances Paxson James (b.1855). A child born c.mid-Oct 1857 and dead at six weeks falls exactly in the gap after Sarah Frances. The only tight parent-couple match in the whole dataset: both parents named, both in the same plot, both of plausible age. No stone.

name: Elijah Holmes
plot_suggested: ? - no Holmes plot of that date
note: The Washingtonian, 22 May 1868: 'Died at his residence near Hamilton, Friday, 1st May, Elijah Holmes in his 72nd year.' Born c.1796-97. The only person in all four sources described as living AT Hamilton. Seven Holmes burials exist across the three cemeteries but the earliest birth is 1884 (Amos Edward Holmes, C-114 Lakeview). Elijah is plausibly that family's ancestor; he is in none of the three.

name: Courtney Newton Carter
note: One of three children of E. L. & M. L. Carter dead of diphtheria in six days, May 1865. The Carter plot C-89 Lakeview holds Edward F. Carter (1857-19 Oct 1865), but he is S/O SUSAN CARTER and died five months later, so he is not one of these three. CAVEAT: the register is county-wide and gives no place, so there is no evidence these children were buried at Hamilton at all. Listed for the record, not as a Hamilton claim.

name: Wm. Wynkoop
note: Dillon list. Thirty-nine Wynkoop burials across the three cemeteries, including Mary Lacy Wynkoop (1821-10 Feb 1897) at Harmony - a near-contemporary. No Wm. Wynkoop of that date on a stone. Surname-and-era only; no corroborating detail.

name: Thos. J. Everhart
note: Register 1866. Twenty-three Everhart burials across plots C-36, C-37, C-90, C-95, C-119. His parents (Jos. & Eliz.) are NOT the C-37 couple (Wm. N. & Catharine), so he does not belong to Annie Arabella's plot. A Joseph/Elizabeth Everhart plot may exist but is not identified here.

name: Henry S. Taylor
note: Register 1866. Born c.1799, son of Bernard Taylor. Not the C-52 family (Lewis Taylor's line). Noted because the Taylor cluster at C-52 is otherwise well resolved and he is the one 1860s Taylor left over.

name: Noble B. Peacock
parents_or_kin: husband of Lucinda Beans Peacock; father of Winfield Scott, Nancy C. and others
note: Surfaced 26 Oct 2026 by the relationship date-check. The register names 'Noble B. & Lucinda Peacock' as the parents of two children who died of scarlet fever in Jan and Feb 1859, both matched to stones at C-54. His wife LUCINDA BEANS PEACOCK (LV0759, 1828-1890) is at C-54, with four of their children: Winfield Scott (LV0760), Nancy C. (LV0761), James Henry (LV0756, 1855-1929) and Lola M. (LV0758, 1853-1897). NOBLE HIMSELF HAS NO STONE in any of the three cemeteries. The only Noble in the data is LV0757 Noble Braden Peacock (1896-1904), a child who died at 8 and was plainly named for him - a grandson, two generations later. A man whose wife and four children lie in one plot is very likely in it too, unmarked or with a lost stone.
